chunks: And the Shaykh — may Allah the Exalted support him — informed me. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed me, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him). He said:
I asked him about a man who urinates but does not wash his penis until he has performed wudu for salat.
He said: 'He should wash his penis, but he does not need to repeat his wudu.'

key_terms.ذَكَرَهُ: his penis/male organ — the body part requiring washing after urination
key_terms.وُضُوءَ: wudu — ritual ablution required before salat; here in the compound 'wudu of salat'
key_terms.يَبُولُ: urinates — the act causing ritual impurity (najasah) requiring washing
key_terms.يُعِيدُ: repeats/redoes — the question of whether the wudu must be invalidated and redone

ai.seo_question: According to Imam Musa al-Kazim, does a man need to repeat his wudu if he performed it without first washing his penis after urination?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a jurisprudential ruling from Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him), transmitted by his trusted companion 'Ali ibn Yaqtin who served in the Abbasid court. The ruling addresses a man who performs wudu for salat without having first washed his penis after urination: the Imam rules that the washing must be performed but the wudu itself is valid and need not be repeated, drawing a distinction between the purification of the organ and the validity of the ablution.
